messages.content: What is the largest planet in the universe?

function.name: space_star_info
function.description: Retrieve information about a particular star in the universe. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

information.description: The type of information needed about the star.

message.content:
The largest planet that has been confirmed so far is **HD 100546 b**.  
It is a protoplanet still forming around the young star HD 100546, located about 335 light‑years from Earth.  Estimates put its radius at roughly 2.5–3 times that of Jupiter (≈ 200,000 km), making it the biggest planet we’ve detected in the observable universe.  

> **Note:** Because HD 100546 b is still in the process of accreting material, its exact size and mass are still being refined.  No larger planet has been confirmed yet, though future observations may reveal even more massive worlds.
